subject.title: fix(config): improve validation error messages with line numbers, bracket paths, and received values

question: What received-value disclosure contract should terminal config validation use when the effective invalid value may come from environment expansion, includes, compatibility normalization, or plugin-owned configuration?
rationale: Accurate hints require consulting the effective validated value, but doing so can reveal resolved credentials or custom plugin secrets; source inspection cannot choose the repository's acceptable disclosure boundary.

options.title: Allow closed safe scalar hints
options.body: Use the effective value only for explicitly approved non-secret scalar cases, suppressing hints when provenance or path sensitivity is uncertain.

options.title: Drop received-value hints
options.body: Merge only line-number and bracket-path improvements, avoiding a new configuration-value disclosure surface.

options.title: Accept heuristic redaction
options.body: Retain broad value hints using the current sensitive-path and SecretRef checks and explicitly accept the remaining custom-path risk.

recommendation.title: Allow closed safe scalar hints
recommendation.body: Use the effective value only for explicitly approved non-secret scalar cases, suppressing hints when provenance or path sensitivity is uncertain.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior config snapshot redaction work is the closest history signal for deciding this disclosure boundary.
